candidates.item: 'Mode' (French/German for fashion) + 'Lab' (laboratory/experimental) — name signals creative experimentation in fashion.
candidates.why_interesting: The studio name is a bilingual pun — 'Mode' means fashion in both French and German, so the name literally translates to 'Fashion Lab' for European-language speakers while reading as a sleek English compound to everyone else. That's a quietly clever piece of naming for a brand-building studio that claims to do naming and brand identity for clients.
candidates.recency_note: Observed in step-1 research; site appears early-stage with no external press footprint.

candidates.item: 'We reply to every serious enquiry within two business days.'
candidates.why_interesting: The word 'serious' is doing real work here — it's a quiet filter that signals selectivity and positions the studio as choosing its clients, not chasing them. That's an unusual stance for an early-stage, no-portfolio studio and reveals a deliberate boutique/exclusive positioning strategy.
candidates.recency_note: Observed in step-1 research; live homepage copy as of research date.

candidates.item: No pricing, no portfolio, no client names mentioned on homepage — early-stage or deliberately exclusive presentation.
candidates.why_interesting: A studio selling brand-building and creative credibility has zero social proof on its own homepage — no clients, no case studies, no team names. That's a bold structural bet: the positioning and copy alone are meant to attract the right clients. It's either a very confident move or a revealing constraint — either way, it's specific and discussable.
candidates.recency_note: Observed in step-1 research; consistent with a new or early-stage venture.

candidates.item: The signup first name is 'Mode' and the contact email is hi@modelab.site — 'Mode' is likely a shortened handle, brand alias, or non-standard first name rather than a legal given name.
candidates.why_interesting: The person or founder goes by the same word as the company's name and the French/German word for fashion — they've essentially merged their identity with the brand. That's an unusually committed personal-brand move (or a deliberate air of mystery), and it means there's no findable founder footprint anywhere online.
candidates.recency_note: Observed in step-1 research; no external corroboration found.
candidates.sensitivity: Could be sensitive if 'Mode' prefers to keep their real identity private — treat as an alias and do not probe for legal name.
